speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying your symptoms: When you feel dizzy, does the room actually spin around you, or do you feel like you are falling? How long does each episode typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To narrow down the cause, does the dizziness occur specifically when you roll over in bed, lean forward, or look up? And have you noticed any hearing loss, tinnitus, or fullness in one specific ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Although you were told it was migraine, your history of position-dependent vertigo without recent illness or significant hearing loss is classic for BPPV. I recommend performing a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis.
